Does anyone have any suggestions on how to go about this?

I have some still-in-development code to fortify output from rq models (quantile regression with the package quantreg, which seems to be the "classic" one). From then on, you would have to write the corresponding autoplot function (which is really:
1. calling fortify
2. calling ggplot() + geom_path() with the appropriate columns from the output of fortify

Hopefully, this, one day, will be in a package.

I paste the below:

fortify.rq <- function(model, data=model$model, ...) {
#
# Extract data from a requession quantile object into a data.frame
#

fitted <- predict(model, ...)
resid <- residuals(model)

# merge with data
res <- data.frame(data, .fitted=fitted, .resid=resid, row.names=NULL)

# identify quantile
res$.tau <- model$tau
res$.tau <- as.factor(res$.tau)

return(res)
}

fortify.rqs <- function(model, data=model$model, ...) {
#
# Extract data from a requession quantile object into a data.frame
#
suppressPackageStartupMessages(require("reshape2", quietly=TRUE))

# get fitted values for all quantiles
fit <- as.data.frame(predict(model))
# convert to long shape
fit <- melt(fit, measure.vars=1:ncol(fit), variable.name=".tau", value.name=".fitted")

# get residuals
resid <- as.data.frame(residuals(model))
resid <- melt(resid, measure.vars=1:ncol(resid), variable.name=".tau", value.name=".resid")
# merge with fit
fit$.resid <- resid$.resid

# identify quantiles
fit$.tau <- model$tau[as.numeric(fit$.tau)]
fit$.tau <- factor(fit$.tau)

# merge with data
res <- data.frame(data, fit, row.names=NULL)

return(res)
}

> 1. calling fortify
> 2. calling ggplot() + geom_path() with the appropriate columns from the output of fortify

Here are the types of plot you may want to do with the output of fortify

md <- fortify(m)

# check the distribution of residuals
ggplot(md) + geom_histogram(aes(x=.resid), binwidth=0.2) + facet_wrap(~.tau)
# a qqplot is also appropriate

# check homoscedasticity
ggplot(md) + geom_point(aes(x=.fitted, y=.resid))

# plot the fit
ggplot(m) + geom_point(aes(x=size, y=TG_Chol)) + geom_line(aes(x=size, y=.fitted, colour=.tau))
# here my x variable is size and my y variable is TC_Chol, this has to be adapted to your variables of course

Here is what I used to generate my plot:

females <- read.csv2("females.csv")

female.weight <- lmsqreg.fit(log(females$heart),
                             log(females$weight),
                             pvec = (centiles <- c(0.03, 0.1, 0.5, 0.9, 0.97)),
                             lam.fixed=1)

###To plot, there are two options:

##1. For evaluation

plot.lmsqreg.fit(female.weight)

##2. for publication

plot(log(females$weight),log(females$heart),
     axes=FALSE,
     frame.plot=TRUE,
     xlab="Weight (kg)",
     ylab="Heart weight (g)",
     main="Women",
     col = "white",
     xlim = c(3.2,5.3))

axis(1,at=log(xat <- c(3,5,7,9,11,13,15,17,19)*10),
     labels=xat)

axis(2,at=log(yat <- (2:7)*100),labels=yat)

lpars <- list(lty=rep(c(2,1,2),
                      c(2,1,2)),
              col=c("#444444","#999999","#000000")
              [c(1,2,3,2,1)])

for(l in 1:nrow(female.weight$qsys$outmat) ){
  lines(female.weight$qsys$targetx,
        female.weight$qsys$outmat[l,],
        lty=lpars$lty[l],col=lpars$col[l])
 
  text(female.weight$qsys$targetx[lx <- length(female.weight$qsys$targetx)],
       female.weight$qsys$outmat[l,lx],
       paste(centiles[l]*100,"%",sep=""),adj=c(-0.5,0.5))
}

Well, google decided to eat my original reply.  So let's try again.

My personal opinion is that autoplot methods should seek to replicate functionality of the original plot() functions.  So you really have two questions, with one (in my opinion) not having much in particular to do with autoplot.

I haven't had much time to work on this (and I burned some of that because I forgot about the aes/aes_string problem), but I've basically replicated the functionality of plot.lmsqreg.fit in ggplot.  I'm not proud of this solution, but I'm not going to have any more time to look over it until at least this weekend, so at least for now, it is what it is.

I had to make some insane choices to get things to work right, but it seems to work ok.  It definitely could stand to be significantly cleaned up.  See attached file.

As for your second plot, hopefully this and Jean-Oliver's posts will show you the way.  It looks like it will be a fairly similar translation going from autoplot() --> custom plot, as you did for  plot() --> custom plot...if that makes sense.

Best of luck.
